falsifier: A row `savedregs --per-web` reports UNRESOLVED whose true mapping is nevertheless derivable from the two streams alone, without reading the aligned view -- i.e. a decision procedure that separates two candidates tied at the same aligned distance in different registers. Producing one would show the refusal is over-cautious. Conversely, a distance-0 candidate that is measurably the WRONG range (check with `fnasm <unit> <fn> 0xA:0xB --diff`) would show distance 0 is not decisive and the shipped rule is too permissive.
subject: tool:savedregs
value:
A LIVE-RANGE PAIRING MADE ON A ROLE STRING MUST NOT BE TIE-BROKEN BY PROXIMITY: WHERE NOTHING SITS AT THE ALIGNED POSITION AND THE CANDIDATES DISAGREE ABOUT THE REGISTER, THE ANSWER IS UNRESOLVED, NOT THE NEAREST ONE.

A role is a short string. `li 0` is the role of every zero-initialisation in a function, so pairing two streams' definitions by role leaves several candidates, and returning the nearest one AS A REGISTER MAPPING publishes a coin-flip in the vocabulary of a measurement. MEASURED on game/anim/action::DoPlayerAction: the target's `@0x88 li r19,0` has exactly two role-matching candidates, r24 and r18, and BOTH sit 24 aligned rows away.

DISTANCE 0 IS THE DISCRIMINANT, AND IT WAS CHOSEN FROM THREE MEASURED CANDIDATES RATHER THAN REASONED TO. Distance 0 means the two definitions occupy the SAME position in the opcode-sequence alignment -- the alignment's own answer, not a ranking. Swept over every live-range row in the tree (17,688 rows, 2,998 function pairs):
  A  refuse only an exact tie at the minimum   3 rows /   3 fns (0.02%)
  B  a UNIQUE candidate at distance 0 decides 98 rows /  52 fns (0.55%)  SHIPPED
  C  refuse any in-window disagreement       389 rows / 115 fns (2.20%)
Under B the census moves PERMUTED 1365->1327, ESCAPED 228->195, INTRUDER 158->134.

THE NEGATIVE SIDE KILLED C, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERED. C turns all four of the rows claim.law.T12_pairing-callee-saved-definitions-by-ordinal-within-a-register-fails-exactly-when-a-lifetime-moves.20260903.v1 names in its EXPIRY CHECK (`--per-web` must keep naming r21->r19 x2 and r19->r12 x2) into refusals, and `fnasm game/movie/movieplayer fn_800D8BCC 0x1c0:0x260 --diff` shows every one of them is CORRECT: target `1c4 li r21,0` against our `1c4 li r19,0`, and the whole r21 range at `22c rlwinm`, `23c addi`, `240 cmpw` against our r19 range at the same offsets. Each has a UNIQUE candidate at distance 0 with its alternatives 4, 1, 22 and 1 rows further out. A refusal rule that discards distance-0 evidence refuses MEASUREMENTS, which is the opposite failure to the one it is built for. A is too narrow: an exact numeric tie is an accident, and 95 pure-proximity mappings survive it.

THE GENERAL FORM: a tool that pairs on a lossy key must report the tie rather than break it, and the SPLIT between 'decidable' and 'guessed' has to be measured against a corpus that already contains verified answers -- otherwise the guard is calibrated only on the cases it should catch, and the ones it should not are exactly where it does damage.
